title: Ecuador - Emergency Resilient Reconstruction Project : The Inspection Panel Notice of Non-Registration on a Request for Inspection
text:
IBRAHIM JAMES PAM
Chairperson
The Inspection Panel




 IPN REQUEST 26/03

 March 27, 2026


 MEMORANDUM TO THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTORS AND ALTERNATES
 INTERNATIONAL BANK FOR RECONSTRUCTION AND DEVELOPMENT

 The Inspection Panel

 Notice of Non-Registration on a Request for Inspection

 Ecuador: Emergency Resilient Reconstruction Project (P181079)


 Summary

 1. In accordance with paragraph 18 of the Resolution of the World Bank Board of Executive
 Directors (the “Board”), the World Bank Accountability Mechanism: Inspection Panel and Dispute
 Resolution Service (the “Resolution”), 1 I hereby inform you that on February 10, 2026, the
 Inspection Panel (the “Panel”) received a Request for Inspection (the “Request”) related to the
 Ecuador: Emergency Resilient Reconstruction Project (P181079) (the “Project”). The Request was
 submitted by the “representatives of the organized community” in Chimborazo, Ecuador, with 115
 signatories. The Request asks for confidentiality for the representatives and signatories “due to
 concerns of potential retaliation.” A redacted copy of the Request for Inspection is attached as
 Annex I.

 2. The Request states the Project would reroute the E35 highway “away from the city,” which
 would effectively isolate the historic Andean city of Alausí from the main national transportation
 corridor, resulting in severe, irreversible, and cumulative economic, social, environmental, and
 safety impacts on the local population. The Request raises serious concerns regarding economic
 isolation, geotechnical risks, and community safety, as well as inadequate consultation with
 affected communities and insufficient assessment of environmental and social risks which could
 potentially threaten livelihoods. The Request asks that the World Bank Inspection Panel conduct
 a formal investigation into this Project and assess its compliance with the World Bank’s
 environmental and social safeguard policies and procedures.

 3. After conducting its initial due diligence, the Panel concluded that the Request does not
 meet one of the admissibility criteria for Registration. The Panel is not satisfied that Management

 has been made aware of the issues raised in the Request prior to its submission to the Panel. I am
therefore notifying you that the Panel is not registering this Request.

The Project

4. The Board approved the Project on May 26, 2023, with a total cost of USD 150 million
financed through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. 2 The implementing
agency is the Ministry of Transport and Public Works – Ministerio de Transporte y Obras Públicas
(MTOP). The current closing date of the Project is June 30, 2028.

5. The Project Development Objective is to restore connectivity and improve infrastructure
resilience and road safety in areas affected by natural hazards. 3 The Project has two components.
The first covers infrastructure recovery and resilience interventions and the second, project
management and institutional strengthening for resilience. At the time of Project approval, all
Environmental and Social Standards of the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework
were considered relevant except for ESS9 on Financial Intermediaries. 4

The Request

6. The Request alleges the Bank-financed intervention related to the E35 national highway
crossing the Chimborazo Province, Ecuador, is expected to generate severe, irreversible, and
cumulative economic, social, environmental, and safety impacts on the local population of the
historic Andean city of Alausí. The Request explains that the city’s economy depends primarily on
tourism, commerce, transportation, and local services directly connected to the E35 highway. It
adds that the rerouting of E35 would effectively isolate Alausí from the main national transportation
corridor, and would, thereby, drastically reduce the flow of visitors, trade, and economic activity,
directly affecting hundreds of local families, small businesses, transport operators, and tourism-
related services.

7. The Request states that the community is still recovering from a catastrophic landslide that
damaged sections of the E35, caused loss of life and displaced families, and precipitated a severe
economic decline. It also states that further isolation could exacerbate the vulnerability of the
population. The Request states that the alternative route proposed would cross “Gampala,” which
is in a mountainous area that is geologically unstable. It also states that construction activities, such
as excavation, the use of heavy machinery, and vibrations, could further increase the risk of
landslides, threatening residents, homes, and infrastructure.

8. Furthermore, the Request claims consultation and stakeholder engagement processes
conducted by national authorities and the MTOP have not adequately included the directly affected
population. It adds that public meetings have been limited and selective, excluding many residents,
business owners, and community members who will bear the impact of the Project. According to
the Request, this raises serious concerns regarding the World Bank’s compliance with its
Environmental and Social Framework.

 Panel’s Observation and Determination

9. In accordance with the Panel’s Operating Procedures, 5 and following its review of
information gathered through its due diligence, the Panel confirms that the Request does not meet
one of the admissibility criteria for Registration. The Panel determines that the Request is not
frivolous, absurd, or anonymous. The Panel also confirms that the Request was submitted by
representatives of 115 signatories located in Ecuador, who claim to be affected by the Project. The
Panel further notes that, since the Project was approved after September 8, 2020, the deadline for
submitting a Request for Inspection is fifteen months after the Project closure date of June 30,
2028. The Panel adds that the subject matter of the Request does not concern issues of procurement
and the Panel has not previously made a recommendation on these issues. During its meeting with
the Panel, the Requesters confirmed that they had not yet contacted Bank Management.

10. Based on the foregoing, the Panel considers that Management was not made aware of the
issues raised in the Request prior to its submission, as set out in paragraph 14 of the Resolution
and paragraph 14(d) of the Operating Procedures. I therefore notify you that the Panel is not
registering this Request.

11. This non-registration does not preclude the possibility of a future Request for Inspection
related to this Project.


 Yours sincerely,




 Ibrahim Pam
 Chairperson

Request for Inspection
 (Redacted)
 DETAILED COMPLAINT

Organized Ecuador

115 Signatories

Request for Full Investigation and Possible World Bank Technical Mission

Harm caused or likely to be caused to the community

The World Bank-financed intervention related to the E35 national highway in Alausí, Chimborazo
Province, Ecuador, is expected to generate severe, irreversible, and cumulative economic, social,
environmental, and safety impacts on the local population.

Alausí is a historic Andean city whose economy depends primarily on tourism, commerce,
transportation, and local services directly connected to the E35 highway, which currently crosses
the urban center. The proposed project would reroute the E35 away from the city, effectively
isolating Alausí from the main national transportation corridor. This would drastically reduce the flow
of visitors, trade, and economic activity, directly affecting hundreds of local families, small
businesses, transport operators, and tourism-related services.

The community of Alausí is still recovering from a catastrophic landslide that destroyed sections of
the E35 highway, caused significant loss of life, displacement of families, and severe economic
decline. Any additional isolation resulting from the rerouting of the highway would further
exacerbate the existing social and economic vulnerability of the population.

The alternative route proposed by national authorities would cross a mountain known locally as
“Gampala,” located directly above the city of Alausí. Independent professionals and local technical
assessments have identified this mountain as geologically unstable and at risk of landslides.
Construction activities such as excavation, heavy machinery operation, and vibration could
destabilize the slope and potentially trigger a major landslide that could threaten the lives, homes,
and infrastructure of residents living on the lower slopes and in the urban center of Alausí.

Furthermore, consultation and stakeholder engagement processes conducted by national
authorities and the Ministry of Transportation and Public Works have not adequately included the
directly affected population. Public meetings have been limited and selective, excluding many
residents, business owners, and community members who will bear the impacts of the project. This
raises serious concerns regarding compliance with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social
Framework.

For these reasons, we respectfully request that the World Bank Inspection Panel conduct a formal
investigation into this project and assess compliance with the World Bank’s environmental and
social safeguard policies and procedures, including the possibility of a technical mission to
Ecuador.
